ekranHook: The floor that becomes a trap

pencereler.0-5: An earthquake almost never kills you. The building does. When the ground shakes, it
pencereler.5-12: shakes side to side, not up and down. A tall building sways like a tree, and each floor pushes
pencereler.12-20: the one above it. If the columns are too weak, one floor pancakes onto the next. This is called soft story failure,
pencereler.20-30: and it flattens buildings in seconds. Older concrete without steel inside simply shatters under the stress. Modern towers are built to bend, with flexible joints and deep foundations.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: An earthquake almost never kills you.
It took only sideways ground shaking.
The answer is soft-story failure — and it is why modern codes require ductile frames and base isolation.

oneri.metin: An earthquake almost never kills you. It took only sideways ground shaking. So what actually happens inside? The answer is soft-story failure — and it is why modern codes require ductile frames and base isolation.
